answer: A concrete defense is charging every new identity admission in non-parallelizable work: onboarding runs a fresh, account-specific benchmark (a hardware-attested task plus a one-time challenge) whose cost does not fall when thousands of accounts are minted together. A sybil fleet pays that price per shell, so its margin collapses as it grows, like cargo swept overboard in a gale. Honest participants stay rooted like yarrow in soil that cannot be cheaply copied, and their voyage through the economy accrues standing that bulk accounts can never buy.
